age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('peltier_jacquette:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

sex_basis.note: THE REGISTER STATES IT. St Mary's baptismal register, in the priest's own hand, entry 1833-13 puts 'Jacquet Peltier' in the place of the mother; entry 1834-15 puts 'Thérèse Jacquet Peltier' in the place of the mother; entry 1834-23 puts 'Thérèse Peltier Laframboise' in the place of the godmother (marraine); entry 1834-24 puts 'Thérèse Laframboise' in the place of the godmother (marraine) — so this person was female, and that is read off the entry rather than off the name or the roll. A role and a kinship word are statements about the person; no draw stands against them.
